study type: Secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study
exposure: synthetic prostaglandin (sPG) exposure for labor induction
non-sPG methods for labor induction (e.g., balloon catheter, amniotomy, oxytocin, laminaria)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 3,071 nulliparous women with singleton pregnancies undergoing induction of labor between 34 0/7 and 42 0/7 weeks of gestation, drawn from the larger nuMoM2b multicenter prospective cohort.
finding: After adjustment for clinical and demographic factors, exposure to synthetic prostaglandins for cervical ripening or labor induction was not significantly associated with newborn respiratory distress syndrome.
